clue.text: Friend in morning dress could be Ernie

indicators.note: the friend sits in the morning, as if wearing it like morning dress, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: A pal dressed in tails and a cravat might be someone called Ernie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morning dress' looks like formal wear; split it, with 'in' as the container signal. ERNIE was the British Premium Bond prize machine, Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment, a name built from initials.
explanation.definitionFit: ERNIE is a name made from the initials of the words it stands for, the very type of word meant.

clue.text: Two scholars in reform school

indicators.note: in places the two scholars inside the word for reform

parts.note: to alter is to reform or change
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar, taken twice
MA again, the second scholar

explanation.surface: Two academics are sent to a borstal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform school' looks like one phrase; split it. Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, is one's old school.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is the term for the college or school one attended.

clue.text: Acceptance of old culinary instructions

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a recipe

explanation.definitionFit: Receipt means the receiving of something and is also an old word for a recipe.

clue.text: A factor in the distribution of intelligence

definitions.text: A factor in the distribution of intelligence

parts.words: A factor in the distribution of intelligence
parts.note: factor in its sense of an agent, intelligence in its sense of news: a shop agent who sells papers

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sociological variable affecting how clever people are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factor' means an agent and 'intelligence' means news.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling papers is the agent through whom the news reaches readers.

clue.text: Cleans up work submitted in manuscript

indicators.note: submitted in says the work piece is placed inside the manuscript

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone tidies an essay handed in as handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to clean up spilled liquid with a cloth.

clue.text: Casual worker getting bad start

indicators.note: the word start says the piece for bad comes at the beginning, ahead of the worker

parts.note: food gone bad is off
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A laid-back employee has a poor first day on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is a casual, careless one.

clue.text: Where drinks may be served when short of money

explanation.definitionFit: A whisky over ice is served this way, and a failing business or marriage is said to be in this state.

clue.text: Individual submerged in shallow water inlet

indicators.note: submerged in says the individual goes inside the shallow water

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing
I is one, an individual

explanation.surface: A person is underwater in a shallow sea inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiord is a long narrow sea inlet between cliffs.

clue.text: Brave tamer in difficulty to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lion-tamer in trouble shows a measure of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is an old word for a Native American warrior, and Amerind is a term for a Native American.

clue.text: Dispute promotion of eccentric journalist

indicators.note: promotion lifts things up, so in a down clue the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: rum means odd or eccentric
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Raising a quirky reporter to a senior post causes argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion of' turns RUMED upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection, to dispute.

clue.text: Bird's jaws without bill

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jaws wrap round the bill

parts.note: a maw is the jaws or mouth of a greedy animal
CA, current account, stands for a bill or account

explanation.surface: A bird's mouth is described as lacking a beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here has its old meaning of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot.

clue.text: Source of power for Euro-MP let loose?

indicators.note: let loose suggests the letters of the two words are set free to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks what fuels a member of the European Parliament once freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' tells you to rearrange EUROMP and LET together.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is a fuel that drives engines and generators.

clue.text: Opening of "Mikado" introducing opera to number in eastern arena

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera
N stands for number in algebra

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a staging of The Mikado brought to a big stage in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' and 'to' just order the pieces: M, then AIDA, then N.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and nearby lands a maidan is an open public ground used for gatherings and sport.

clue.text: Daredevil not very bothered though carrying more risk

indicators.note: bothered as in flustered or agitated, signalling the remaining letters are jumbled
not very says the letter for very is to be dropped from the word daredevil

explanation.surface: A stuntman is unworried even though his act is getting more perilous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' removes V from DAREDEVIL, leaving DAREDEIL, which 'bothered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: something with greater potential to kill carries more risk.

clue.text: Father upset mother perhaps? Extremely likely so it seems

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so father is read upwards

parts.note: Pa is father
a mother is an example of a parent

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of likely

explanation.surface: Dad is distressed that Mum seems very probably involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PA to AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently means seemingly, by appearances.

clue.text: The right name

definitions.meaning: a legal entitlement to property, as in holding the deeds
the heading or name of a book or film

explanation.definitionFit: A title is both a legal right of ownership and the name given to a work.

clue.text: Fodder for one who sells by word of mouth

indicators.note: spoken rather than written, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: for gives PRO, and one who sells is a vendor

explanation.surface: Asks what feed a street seller would hawk by shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO VENDOR said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is dry food for animals such as horses, an old word for feed.

clue.text: Place most disturbed by psychic emanation

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A location was most upset by a ghostly presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges PLACE and MOST together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance said by spiritualists to come from a medium.

clue.text: Stand for soldiers' salute

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers
present arms is a military salute

explanation.surface: An order for troops to come to attention and salute.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent is to stand for or symbolise.

clue.text: Where to run champion dog

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an ace is a champion or expert
to dog someone is to track or follow them

explanation.surface: Where you would race a prize-winning greyhound.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and also the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit for greyhound racing is exactly where a top dog runs.

clue.text: About to stir drink excessively

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
to rouse is to stir or awaken

explanation.surface: Someone is about to wake up and hit the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink heavily and make merry.

clue.text: Carry on trading initially in crash

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the carrying piece after the first letter
initially means take the opening letter of trading

parts.note: to hump is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: Advice to keep doing business even as the market collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' looks like a phrase meaning continue; split it, with 'on' placing HUMP after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A thump is a heavy blow or the dull sound of something crashing down.

clue.text: Universal hymn to send on high

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal
a hymn is a song of praise

explanation.surface: A hymn sung by all lifts the spirits heavenward.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is to lift up or raise aloft.

clue.text: Took off for hurried round tour

indicators.note: round says the hurried word goes around the outside of the tour word

parts.note: sped means hurried
a trip is a tour or journey

explanation.surface: Someone departed on a rushed circuit of sightseeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like 'departed'; here it means removed clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To have taken off one's clothes is to have undressed.

clue.text: Hold inquiry concerning delay

definitions.meaning: to deliberate on a case as a jury does
to hold back or suppress something

explanation.definitionFit: A committee may sit on a case to investigate, and an official may sit on a report to hold it up.

clue.text: It supplements seed for bird

indicators.note: supplements means is added on, so it goes after the seed

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: Something added to birdseed is offered as feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seed for bird' looks like birdseed; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small brown songbird like a lark.

clue.text: Plant left out of extravagant display

indicators.note: left out of means the letter for left is removed from the word for showy spending

parts.note: a splurge is a lavish display or spending spree

explanation.surface: Something was omitted from an over-the-top show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes L from SPLURGE. Spurge is a family of plants with milky sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge is the common name for euphorbia plants.

clue.text: Wilde, for example, accepting royal command

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the wit holds the royal letter

parts.note: Oscar Wilde is a famous example of a wit
R stands for royal, as in Rex or Regina

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde takes on an order from the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a written court order or command.

clue.text: Drink to safe end of flight when placed in front of Jumbo, perhaps

indicators.note: when placed in front says the end letter of flight comes first
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: rum is a spirit drink
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A toast to a secure landing for a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jet; it is an elephant, which trumpets. 'when placed in front' puts the T at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant such as Jumbo makes a loud brassy call, so is one that trumpets.

clue.text: Few in drink are so animated

indicators.note: in places the small number inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
a few, here four, written IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A handful of people at the pub are lively.
explanation.walkthrough: IV, four as a Roman numeral, stands loosely for a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alive is being lively and full of energy.

clue.text: Right of passage denied to none prepared to make the attempt

indicators.note: prepared in the sense of made ready or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to try is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Nobody is allowed through, so nobody even bothers to try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges NONE to NOEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign forbidding entry means passage is refused.

clue.text: A serious blow incurred in play

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's late play set on an island, opening in a storm

explanation.definitionFit: Tempest means a violent storm and is also the title of a Shakespeare play.
